title: Apple Stock's Biggest Bull Is Less Bullish After 'Horror Show' - Barron's
text:
Apple Stock’s Biggest Bull Is Less Bullish After ‘Horror Show’ By Nov. 28, 2018 10:11 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Spencer Platt/Getty Images Text size
One of the most bullish Apple (AAPL) stock analysts on Wall Street is now a bit less optimistic on the smartphone maker.
Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives lowered his price target on Apple shares to $275 from $310, citing the lack of transparency from the company. The prior $310 target was previously the highest on the Street. The analyst’s new price forecast is now the third highest out of 40 firms that cover Apple, according to FactSet, and the current high is $300.
“We fully acknowledge the XR/XS iPhone cycle has been a clear disappointment with demand in the U.S., China, Japan, and India all translating into a declining unit year in FY19,” he wrote on Wednesday. “While the stock over the next 3 to 6 months will likely trade at the low end of its historical P/E range given the soft iPhone cycle and lack of transparency around iPhone metrics, we do believe this will be relatively short-lived.”
As a result of weaker iPhone demand, the analyst reduced his Apple fiscal 2019 earnings-per-share estimate to $13.52 from $13.90, versus the $13.39 Wall Street consensus.
Despite the weak data points, Ives is still bullish about Apple shares for the long term and reaffirmed his Outperform rating for the stock. The analyst cited the company’s iPhone active installed base of more than 750 million devices and rising services revenue.
“Apple still remains of our favorite tech names heading into 2019 despite the horror show over the last month seen out of Cupertino,” he wrote. “Our bullish thesis on Apple for the coming years … remains unchanged.”
Listen to a conversation between tech reporter Tae Kim and Alex Eule about IBM’s attempted reboot as well as Apple’s predicaments in a recent episode of The Readback. You can sign up for the podcast in iTunes or wherever you listen to podcasts .
Apple stock is up $2.05, or 1.18%, to $176.29 in Wednesday morning trading.
Last week, The Wall Street Journal , citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple has cut orders in recent weeks for all three newly released iPhone models.
Apple stock has fallen about 20% this month as investors have grown increasingly worried about iPhone sales.
Earlier this month, wireless-chip maker Qorvo (QRVO) reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter, citing weaker demand for high-end smartphones. And iPhone suppliers Lumentum Holdings (LITE) and Japan Display (6740.Japan) lowered their financial forecasts on Nov. 12.
